heroHeadline: AFP Finds No Confirmed Drilling by Chinese Survey Vessel at Scarborough Shoal; Weekly Tally Counts 48 Chinese Vessels Across Four WPS Features
heroSubtitle: AFP Special Spokesperson for the West Philippine Sea, Rear Admiral (ret./res.) Roy Vincent Trinidad, said on September 15, 2026 that the Chinese drilling-capable survey vessel Haiyang Dizhi Shihao's roughly 28-day presence off Bajo de Masinloc (Scarborough Shoal) showed movement patterns consistent with surveillance or research, with 'no confirmed' drilling activity detected by AFP monitoring. The same briefing disclosed AFP's weekly West Philippine Sea vessel tally for September 8-14, 2026: 48 Chinese coast guard and naval vessels across four contested features — Ayungin (Second Thomas) Shoal, Bajo de Masinloc, Escoda (Sabina) Shoal, and Pag-asa (Thitu) Island. It follows the September 8 AFP assessment that Chinese pressure across Batanes, Scarborough Shoal and Ayungin Shoal forms a 'synchronized, persistent' campaign, the September 7 incident in which Chinese forces fired flares at an unarmed Philippine Coast Guard patrol aircraft near Subi and Mischief Reefs, and the September 8 Seoul Defense Dialogue episode in which a Chinese embassy note was handed to Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. onstage, which he read aloud and called 'coercion, bullying and aggression.'
